rv.q: Harold Brighouse's Zack is a delightful rediscovered comedy of character with many colorful roles which actors can sink their teeth into.
At a cultural moment when empathy feels alarmingly scarce, Zack’s sweet humanity lands with unexpected force.
This time it’s plucked a British play written in 1916 by Harold Brighouse called Zack.
Here, though, the issues feel plotted and schematic rather than developing organically from the characters.
Even when the loosey goosey narrative beats feel arbitrary, the writers at least keep it funny and light.

cn.t: Critics find this rare Brighouse revival a charming but minor work that lacks the heft of his classic "Hobson's Choice," with mixed reactions to the Mint Theater's production.
